project.purpose: Block one of every rich card: the project path below Options.Group, directories plain, ` / ` between segments, the project name linked.

status.purpose: The one bold line: lamp, then Pipeline #n · phrase / MR !n · State / N commits pushed. The phrase names the stage that failed or is running in the stage's own case; sentence() capitalises only the first letter.

title.purpose: The commit title on a pipeline (omitted when empty) or the MR title; clipped at 72 runes; <s> when the MR is closed. A push has no title.

ref.purpose: One <code> run: the branch or tag, or `source → target` on an MR; plain anchors beside it (` · MR !42`, ` · ↰ child of #9`) on a pipeline. Also file names, diff positions, and the 7-character SHA chip nested inside its link (shaChip).

person.purpose: `Opened by <who>` under the MR ref chip; the pusher's name alone under the push branch. A mapped user is a tg://user mention.

stage.purpose: Stage name through sentence() after its aggregated lamp on the stage row; never linked. The jobs row beneath is plain inline text with linked job names; table cells take inline text only.

clock.purpose: htmlfmt.Clock m:ss / h:mm:ss on the stage row; `—` for a skipped or canceled stage; empty until something finished.

body.purpose: MR fact lines (merged/closed, pipeline, conflicts, discussions, approvals while open), the push pipeline line, the plain frozen line, the downstream line, the quiet summary, the paragraphs inside a fold.

live.purpose: The running job on the jobs line. Nothing else is italic.

struck.purpose: Skipped and canceled jobs, a closed MR's title, a deleted branch, a deleted file in the diff fold.

summary.purpose: A label, counted when it can be: `Error · last lines`, `Logs · current stage`, `View changes and description`, `3 files changed · +42 −18`, `1 comment`, `Jobs`.

log.purpose: The last lines of one job, only inside the one log fold; ANSI-stripped, capped by pipelines.log_tail.

meta.purpose: Closing small print ending in `Updated HH:MM`; pipelines also `who · commit 8f6ded0 · 📦 Artifacts: job size`; MR change fragments (`approved by X`).

button.purpose: Capitalised verb; ` ↗︎` (U+2197 U+FE0E) suffix on URL buttons, bare on callbacks; two per row.

grammar.medium: Telegram rich message HTML (Bot API 10.1+): footer, p, b, i, s, code, a, table compact with td align=right (cells take inline text only), details/summary (open or closed), pre with <code class="language-log">, blockquote expandable. Built by htmlfmt.Doc block by block; Message.Keyboard is a normal inline keyboard. No h4, mark, ul, tg-button, reactions. Classic Bot API HTML (htmlfmt.Builder, 4096 minus 200 margin, `… read more`) remains for the pending inheritors.

limit.truncation: whole blocks dropped from the end until the joined blocks fit; the first block is never dropped

head: footer project
p lamp status
p title (pipeline, MR)
p ref chip
footer person (MR, push)

pipeline: table compact stages (quiet: p summary; verbose: + details Jobs)
details log (open Error · last lines | closed Logs · current stage)
footer who · commit sha7 · 📦 Artifacts · Updated HH:MM
mr: blockquote expandable description first line (200 runes)
p mock lines (merged/closed, pipeline, conflicts, 💬 discussions, Approvals while open)
details View changes and description (p full description; p N files changed · +A −D + file chips; p Approvals (merged/closed) · Reviewers (approved) · Assignees · Labels)
footer change by who · Updated HH:MM
push: p Superseded by a newer push | Branch deleted (plain text, no lamp)

statusPhrases.rule: sentence(): stage names keep their own case; only the phrase's first letter is capitalised (`Failed in test`, `Deploy running`, `Waiting for manual: deploy`); the table's stage names go through the same function.

lamps.warning: ⚠️ (passed with warnings, failed allowed, force push)
lamps.pending: ⏳ (created, pending, preparing, waiting; `queued` on a pipeline line)
lamps.push: ↗︎ (U+2197 U+FE0E; the same text glyph ends URL buttons)
lamps.rule: A lamp never stands alone and never trails: it precedes the status run, the stage name, or the fact phrase it judges; a reviewer's approval is the word (approved); frozen-push lines carry no lamp.
lamps.unused: 👤 👥 🏷 🔗 🔒 exist in emoji.go for the pending inheritors and appear on no rich card

stageTable.jobsRow: job · job — plain inline text with linked job names; cells take inline text only
stageTable.aggregate: running > queued > failed > canceled > manual > scheduled > skipped > warning > passed
stageTable.clock: htmlfmt.Clock: first start to last finish once every job is terminal, else sum of finished durations, else empty; `—` for a wholly skipped or canceled stage
stageTable.jobs: linked names; hard failures first with (reason) unless script_failure; running <i>; skipped and canceled <s>; (allowed to fail), (manual); uniform stage → skipped | canceled | waiting | manual: a, b

logFold.failed: Error · last lines (open) — first hard-failed job with a tail, once the pipeline is terminal
logFold.running: Logs · current stage (closed) — the running job's tail
logFold.max: one per card; none in quiet mode; passed jobs have no log

blockquoteExpandable: MR description first line, clipped at 200 runes (mentions rewritten)
push commit list (sha7 title · author, +N more)
details: log fold (open on failure, closed while running)
MR View changes and description (full description; N files changed · +A −D with file chips from MRState.Diff; Approvals when merged/closed, Reviewers (approved), Assignees, Labels)
push diff: N files changed · +A −D (file chips; old → new; (new); deleted struck; +N more; (partial))

mrOrder: 🟣 Merged by X into tgt | 🔴 Closed by X
<lamp> Pipeline #n word [· N failed] [· N manual] (⏳ … queued while pending)
💬 N unresolved threads | 💬 Discussions resolved (whenever threads are enriched, every state)
Approvals n/m · names (open only; folded otherwise)
push: Superseded by a newer push | Branch deleted (plain text)
pipeline: ⏸️ Waiting for manual: job, job (quiet mode only)

footer.meta: pipeline: who · commit sha7 · 📦 Artifacts: job size · Updated HH:MM; MR: change by who · Updated HH:MM; push: Updated HH:MM; branch deleted: none
footer.updated: the card's last event time in Options.Location, HH:MM

pipeline: Open pipeline ↗︎ + Cancel (active, Caps pipeline:cancel) | Retry (failed or canceled, Caps pipeline:retry)
Play <job> per manual job (blocked, Caps job:play)
<job> log ↗︎ per failed job, max 3, skipping the job whose log is on the card
push: Compare ↗︎ (both SHAs real) + Create MR ↗︎ (non-default branch, not superseded)
Run pipeline (no pipeline linked, not superseded, Caps ref:run)

pendingInheritors: push.go TagPush (classic HTML, prose sentence with a bold actor and a Tag button)
grammar.shaChip: shaChip(sha, url): sha[:7]; bare without a URL; used in the commit list and the pipeline meta footer

↗︎ N commits pushed: branch • by @user

; commits quote (sha7 title(48) - author);
; footer 'N files changed · +A −D' over a compact table path | +A −D;
; footer pipeline line, frozen line, daily tagline
body: blockquote expandable: sha7 title per commit, +N more
details 'N files changed · +A −D' over <pre><code class="language-diff"> in git diff --stat shape with per-file counts and totals
footer 'Superseded by a newer push' | 'Branch deleted' when frozen

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Five-Line Head"** Gitgram owns no canvas, no colour and no font. Its surface is a Telegram rich message (Bot API 10.1+, built block by block through `htmlfmt.Doc`) plus a normal inline keyboard, drawn by whichever client and theme the reader chose. The design system is a text grammar: which fact sits in which block, which block is small, which is bold, which is monospace, which folds, which is a button. The world is the user's own five mocks, transcribed in `.impeccable/surfaces/internal-render.md`, and the build follows them line for line. Every pipeline, merge request and push card opens with the same head, read top to bottom in one glance on a phone: a small `
` project line (`client / pokemod / agent`, the configured group stripped, segments joined by ` / `, the project name linked); a bold status line led by one lamp whose phrase names what matters (`❌ Pipeline #5981 · Failed in test`, `🟣 MR !42 · Merged`, `↗︎ 7 commits pushed`); the object's title as a plain paragraph; a `` chip for the ref (`feat/ssaid-grant · MR !42`, `feat/ssaid-grant → develop`, the branch); and a small `
` for the person (`Opened by Ada Lovelace`, the pusher). Below the head the body is the object's evidence: a `` of stages with a clock time right-aligned on each stage row and the jobs as plain linked text on the row beneath, one `
` log fold, an expandable quote for the first line of prose (description, commits), a `
` fold for the rest (`View changes and description`, `3 files changed · +42 −18`, `1 comment`), one paragraph of `
`-separated facts on an MR, a pipeline line on a push. A closing `
` holds the small print: who ran it, the commit as a 7-character code chip, the artifacts, `Updated HH:MM`. The keyboard is plain: two buttons per row, `↗︎` on every button that leaves Telegram, verbs bare (`Retry`, `Cancel`, `Play deploy:cdn`, `Run pipeline`). The build refuses the category default: the emoji-stat rows and the sentence bot (`emi pushed 3 commits to develop in group/sub/project`), and it also refuses the previous world's devices: no `

`, no ``, no `
    `, no in-text buttons, no bot reactions and no reaction controls. Status emoji appear only where the mocks draw them: on the status line, on stage rows, and on the fact lines that carry a state (`✅ Pipeline #5981 passed`, `🟣 Merged by Linus`, `💬 Discussions resolved`); a frozen push says `Superseded by a newer push` in plain text. Output is deterministic (same state, same bytes) so edits are hash-skipped. Note, issue, tag, release and deployment cards still speak classic Bot API HTML and are pending inheritors of this grammar.
keyCharacteristics:
Fixed five-line head on every rich card: project `
`, bold status `

`, title `

`, `` ref `

`, person `

`; slots a card has nothing for are omitted, never left blank.

One bold run per card, and it is the status line: lamp, space, `Object anchor · Phrase`; the phrase names the stage that failed or is running, the MR state, or what the push did, with the stage name in its own case and only the phrase's first letter capitalised (`sentence()`).

One separator: ` · ` (space, middle dot, space) joins fragments everywhere (status line, ref line, footers, summaries, fact lines); ` / ` joins only the project path; ` → ` joins only source and target.
Stages are a `` with two rows per stage: `lamp Stage` with the clock (`m:ss`) right-aligned, then the jobs as plain text with linked names; table cells take inline text only.
One log fold per pipeline card: `Error · last lines` open once failed, `Logs · current stage` closed while running; the log is `<pre><code class="language-log">`.

Two folds: `<blockquote expandable>` for one line of prose (the MR description's first line, the commit list) and a closed `<details>` for the rest: `View changes and description` on an MR, `3 files changed · +42 −18` on a push, `1 comment`, `Jobs`.

`<code>` carries refs, file names, diff positions and the 7-character commit SHA chip inside its link; `<i>` marks only the running job; `<s>` marks only what will not happen (skipped and canceled jobs, a closed MR's title, a deleted branch, a deleted file).

Two `
`s of small print: the project line at the top and the closing meta line (`who · commit 8f6ded0 · 📦 Artifacts: … · Updated HH:MM`), plus the person line under the ref chip.
A normal inline keyboard, two buttons per row, `↗︎` (U+2197 U+FE0E, text presentation) on every URL button and never on a callback button; a card with nothing to do has no keyboard.

Lamps are the only emoji: pipeline and job states (✅ ❌ ⚠️ 🔄 ⏳ ⏸️ ⏭️ 🚫 🕒), MR states (🟢 📝 🟣 🔴), push kinds (↗︎ 🌱 🗑️, ⚠️ force), and four markers (💬 threads, ⚔️ conflict, 📦 artifacts, 🏷️ tag ref) with the two relation arrows (↳ downstream, ↰ parent).

rules.name: The Lamp Beside Its Word Rule
rules.body: A lamp never stands alone and never trails. On the status line it precedes the bold run; on a stage row it precedes the bold stage name; on a fact line it precedes the phrase it judges (`✅ Pipeline #5981 passed`, `💬 2 unresolved threads`, `⚔️ Conflicts with develop`). A reviewer's approval is a word, `Linus (approved)`, not a glyph.

rules.name: The Lamps Are The Only Emoji Rule
rules.body: Status lamps on status lines and stage rows, state lamps on fact lines, four markers and two arrows. Frozen-push lines (`Superseded by a newer push`, `Branch deleted`) are plain text. No decorative glyphs, no person or people icons, no glyphs on buttons, no reactions. `👤 👥 🏷 🔗 🔒` exist in `emoji.go` for the pending inheritors and appear on no rich card.

rules.name: The One Bold Line Rule
rules.body: `` wraps the status line's run (`Pipeline #5981 · Failed in test`) and the stage names in the table; the only other bold is a note author inside the comments fold (`Linus:`) and a stage header inside the verbose `Jobs` fold. The title, ref, footers, fact lines and buttons are never bold.

rules.name: The Phrase Names The Stage Rule
rules.body: The status phrase says where, not just what: `Failed in test`, `Deploy running`, `Waiting for manual: deploy`. Stage names keep the case GitLab gave them; `sentence()` capitalises only the first letter of the phrase, and the same function capitalises the stage name in the table so `Failed in test` points at the `Test` row.

rules.name: The Middle Dot Rule
rules.body: ` · ` is the only fragment separator: on the status line, the ref line, the footers, the fact lines, the summaries and the jobs row. The project path uses ` / ` and the branch movement ` → `; nothing uses ` • `, ` - `, `|` or `,` between fragments (commas belong inside a list of names: `manual: deploy:cdn, deploy:prod`, `Reviewers Linus, Tom`).

rules.name: The Chip Is One Code Run Rule
rules.body: The ref line's chip is a single `<code>` span: `feat/ssaid-grant`, or `feat/ssaid-grant → develop` with the arrow inside the code. Anchors beside it (`MR !42`, `child of #9`) are plain links outside the code. A commit is the opposite nesting: the `<code>` chip sits inside the `<a>`.

rules.name: The Same Head Rule
rules.body: Project, status, title, ref, person, in that order, on every rich card; a slot the object lacks is skipped, and the body never begins before the person line.

rules.name: The Clock Column Rule
rules.body: The stage table's last cell is `align="right"` and is emitted even when empty, so the clock times form one column the eye runs down; a skipped or canceled stage shows `—` there rather than nothing. Cells hold inline text only.

rules.name: The Mock's Lines Stay Out Rule
rules.body: Outside the MR's fold only the lines the mock draws appear: how it ended, its pipeline, conflicts, discussions, and approvals while open. Reviewers, assignees, labels, the diff and the full description live inside `View changes and description`.

rules.name: The Frozen Card Rule
rules.body: A superseded push card says so in a plain line above the footer, drops `Create MR ↗︎` and `Run pipeline`, and keeps `Compare ↗︎`; nothing above the line is rewritten.

rules.name: The Keyboard Is Two Wide Rule
rules.body: Two buttons per row; the destination first (`Open pipeline ↗︎`, `Compare ↗︎`), the operation second (`Retry`, `Create MR ↗︎`); further operations on their own rows below. A single button sits alone on its row.

rules.name: The One Fold Opens Rule
rules.body: Only the log fold ever opens by itself, and only on failure (`Error · last lines`); while running it is closed (`Logs · current stage`); everything else folds closed.

rules.name: The Two Folds Rule
rules.body: A line of prose folds into `<blockquote expandable>`; a labelled thing folds into `<details>` whose summary is the count when there is one (`3 files changed · +42 −18`, `1 comment`) or the name of what it holds (`View changes and description`). If a reader must expand to learn whether something failed, the card is wrong.

rules.name: The Log Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: A `<pre>` block is only ever a job log, only ever inside the one log fold, only for the first hard-failed job or the running job; passed jobs have no log. Lines are ANSI-stripped, section markers dropped, capped by `pipelines.log_tail` (`lines`, `live_lines`, default 10).
